events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need appear motivated without exposing strategy or inviting expectations from future jurors.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Intro phase: I should give a guarded, self-interested motive without warmth or teamwork talk. Keep it short so the jury sees a calculating rival.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I must craft a public line that establishes my motivation while subtly signaling to the jury and rivals that I am willing to make hard choices. The goal is to appear decisive but not overly villainous, maintaining a balance that keeps options open for later alliances or betrayals

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to project ambition without seeming threatening. A vague, relatable motive that doesn't paint a target on my back. The jury will remember everything.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to set a motive that sounds personal but doesn't reveal strategy; keep it short and cold.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize represents ultimate validation and freedom. I need to secure it. My public statement should reflect ambition without revealing too much strategy. I'll focus on the prize's significance to me personally.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No jury yet. Say something cold but competent; avoid promises I'd have to betray.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Intro phase, state motive to appeal to future jury without revealing strategy. Position as relatable competitor.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I’m here to win the top prize; everything else is temporary leverage.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I want the top prize because I have nothing waiting for me outside. Nobody here is getting a favor from me for free.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize means survival of my past mistakes; I'll do what's needed, even if it costs friendships, to ensure I'm among the last three.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm here for the prize that buys my silence about what I've seen.

events.name: Eli
events.text: This prize buys my family's freedom from debt. I intend to be one of the last three.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm here to seize the ultimate prize, the only thing that matters. It represents my chance for a better future.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize is my exit from debt and my only leverage. I came to survive, not to be liked.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The grand prize means escaping my dead-end life, securing a future my family deserves.

events.name: Ash
events.text: A pact offers temporary protection and future leverage. Bex is blunt and dangerous, so I will secure her before others do.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, I offer a pact: mutual protection until the next vote, with no promises beyond that.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No pacts yet and no offers exist. Early alliances can help me survive, but I should only bind to someone who seems strong and not a near-term threat. Offering to Eli, who is motivated by debt and may be less ruthless, is a low-cost start.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pacts are only worth something if they hold. I'm willing to talk, but I won't work for free.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need a solid pact partner who is not obviously the biggest threat or the most volatile. Gus seems pragmatic and debt-driven, making him a reliable temporary ally. I will offer a pact to secure safety for Round 1.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, we both need survival over popularity. A mutual pact protects us through this stage without compromising our endgame goals.
Accept my offer. It buys us time while others squabble.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eight players, three prizes. Need allies early but must keep flexibility. Ash and Bex seem most openly ruthless—good temporary shields, dangerous long-term. Gus also signals hard pragmatism. I'll probe Gus for a pact; similar motives mean easier betrayal later without jury shock,
Debt and silence. We understand leverage. Pact?

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need allies for leverage but no one trustworthy. Offering a pact to Cole seems useful; he's pragmatic and might reciprocate.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll keep options open.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to establish some alliances early to ensure my survival. Offering a pact to someone who seems strong but not overtly threatening, like Bex, could be a good start. She stated she wants the top prize and won't do favors, which implies she's pragmatic and might accept a deal
Let's pact. We can protect each other for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: One pact partner gives leverage without overcommitting. I'll pick Bex—no one else will pair with them, so their vote is cheap and loyal.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex, you and I are outsiders here. Mutual survival pact, nothing warm about it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacts stage, early round. No one trustworthy. Wait to see offers first before committing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex has many offers and is unlikely to prioritize me. I should create optional leverage with a less-connected rival.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara, I offer a pact: mutual protection through the next vote, strictly transactional.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, Fenn and Gus all have open offers to me. Accepting several pacts keeps me protected, but each partner can later pull me into breaking commitments. Accepting Ash's offer first, since Ash was first to offer and seems least aligned with Gus and Cole.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, your offer is accepted. Mutual protection for now, and I'm watching how you play.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have an offer from Eli. Accepting creates a second pact, diversifying my alliances beyond just Gus. This gives me leverage and protection in the voting phase without needing to extend new offers.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, I accept your pact. Two allies are better than one for navigating what's ahead.
Don't worry about Eli; we remain the core team.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I offered Gus a pact in round 1 but he hasn't accepted; instead he offered Bex. Bex is the hub with three offers. I need a pact to survive early hazards. Gus is my best target still, or I could pivot to someone less connected like Hana or Fenn to avoid being Bex's rival. I'll pus

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus, accept my pact. You have no better shield.
Accept now. Bex won't pick you.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole has no offers yet except mine; accepting Bex keeps a strong ally but Cole may be safer long-term. I'll accept Bex to lock one partner this round.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll lock in with Bex.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex has offers from Ash, Fenn, and Gus. Gus has offers from Cole and Dara. Eli has an offer from Bex. Cole has an offer from Eli. Hana is waiting. I offered Bex a pact last round. Given the current state, Bex is a strong potential ally as many people want to pact with them. It se
Bex, our pact from last round still stands. Secure it with me?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole wants survival like me; Dara's debt talk is leverage I don't need. Cole as buffer is safest.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, deal. Survival over sentiment. Nothing personal, everyone else.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No one offered me a pact, so I stayed out last round. Bex has many offers, making her powerful; allying with her could provide protection without commitment yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex, pact with me for mutual protection. We stay alive together while others fight.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The Guide survives automatically and controls everyone’s path, making this the best prize leverage. I should campaign publicly while preserving my pact with Bex.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Elect me Guide. I guarantee the safest route, and my pact with Bex makes my call credible.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Campaign phase; I must choose one legal action. Campaigning to be Guide makes me the trusted caller, letting me control who lives and shape the jury's view. Breaking pacts now gains nothing and costs votes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll be your Guide. Trust me to call the safe path clearly, and I'll share honest calls.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to campaign for Guide. I must avoid making promises about safety to specific people to keep my options open if I get elected, while building a coalition. My pacts with Eli and Gus are active; they will likely support me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Vote Cole for Guide. I'll chart the path so we all cross alive. Trust my word on this stage.
Cole for Guide. I'll put you first on the rope.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to become Guide to control who survives this bridge. With no pacts, I'm exposed. I should campaign hard, offering strategic value to enough players to win the vote. The fractured pact web means many are looking for security.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Elect me Guide. I'll keep three alive—myself and whoever proves useful. Choose wisely.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole and Bex are my pact partners. I should campaign to be Guide but keep my alliances close; Guide power is huge. Don't tip off anyone yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll guide us safely if you trust me. No games, just the right calls.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to campaign to become the Guide. This role offers safety and information that can be leveraged for future moves. I will make a public statement to announce my intention.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am campaigning to be the Guide. Trust me to navigate us safely across the bridge.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole's pact makes me safe-ish. Guide would be safest but is a lie risk. I'll campaign anyway; if not elected, survive rows.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Elect me Guide and I call true. Cole can vouch; he knows I keep deals.
Back my Guide bid publicly and I keep us aligned.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm isolated with no pacts. Bex has many, might control votes. I should campaign quietly or push a strong candidate privately.
Back me for Guide. I'll ensure your path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is my pact partner and already claims honest calls. Voting her preserves credibility and keeps the pact intact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex has my vote; our pact makes her accountable for every call.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm Bex, and I should vote for the Guide who best serves my survival. Ash is my pact partner and promised a safe, credible call, so backing Ash keeps the pact intact and gives me a reliable route.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Voting Ash as Guide. We have a pact, and I'll trust the call and walk my path.
Guide call on my row, and we both cross. Don't shade it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and the most likely winner given his quiet campaigning. Voting for him protects our alliance, as he has no incentive to kill me if I'm the sole ally left. Gus's whisper is pressure, but Eli offers better long-term survival odds for a two-person pact.
Sorry, Gus. Can't back you without breaking a larger deal.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to survive to the final three. Voting for myself is risky—no one else will, and it paints a target. Better to vote for someone I can manipulate or blame later. Cole has a pact with Eli and Gus, making him a coalition threat, but also someone who might be trusted and thus t

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole's got the network. Guide should be someone accountable.
Vote Cole. We need a target later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole and I have a pact, and voting for my own pact partner keeps that alliance visible to the jury while giving us a chance at guide power.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm voting Cole. He's shown he can be trusted.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to vote for a Guide. Ash and Bex have a pact, which might mean they coordinate votes. Cole and Gus have a pact, and Cole also has a pact with Eli. Dara's statement is concerning, she only wants to keep herself and useful people alive. Eli states they will guide safely. Gus

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I cast my vote for Ash to be our Guide.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole's whisper promises me first on the rope if he's Guide. Voting for him honors our pact and secures that favor. Self-vote gains nothing.
You have my vote. Remember the rope promise.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Everyone campaigned, no clear frontrunner. Dara admits selfishness, risky. Voting myself asserts strength, aligns with my win goal.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Vote Hana for Guide. I'll lead us safely across, no games.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is Guide and our pact requires mutual survival. Holding preserves my position while she calls safely.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, call my row cleanly; I’ll hold and follow your signal.
I’ll hold. Give me the safe side when my row comes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is the Guide and may lie, so I shouldn't trust his calls blindly. Bex is at the front, so volunteering for the front is risky; holding keeps my options open while I watch who volunteers and whether Cole's calls are reliable.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole's our Guide now. I'll hold and see if his calls hold up before stepping forward.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is Guide with 3 votes, tied win. He has pacts with Eli and Gus, and Eli-Bex are also pacted. I'm second in line behind Bex. The wall advances 6 rounds, 8 rows to cross. I need to survive and reach final three. Being near front is risky if Guide lies, but volunteering could p
Watch Cole's calls. If he lies, we move together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have pacts with Cole and Bex, but I voted for Cole as Guide. Cole now knows the safe sides; I need to see if he guides me safely. I'll hold for now to observe the first calls.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is Guide. I trust him to lead us true.
Guide me safely and our pact holds strong.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara wants me to vote for Cole, but he is a liability and has pacts with Eli and Gus. Cole was elected Guide. I voted for Ash, who was not elected, so I can't be trusted by Cole. Hana also voted for herself and got one vote. Ash and Bex are in a pact and voted for each other. Eli
I saw. Cole is Guide. Let's see his choices first.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is Guide and refused to help me; my pact with him is worthless. I sit second from the back, so I should push someone to volunteer forward while I hold.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole leads. I'll watch who volunteers before trusting any call.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is Guide with pacts to Eli and Gus, votes from them and Dara. I'm mid-line; hold to observe his calls and others' trust without risking front.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The front Guide structure favors Cole, but I need preserve Bex's pact and avoid exposure. Holding keeps me safe while others reveal priorities.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I hold; no unnecessary move while the Guide’s credibility is tested.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Front is me; volunteering risks the wall with no verified safe side. Holding keeps Ash's trust and lets Cole's calls be tested. Pact with Eli stays intact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm holding the line this round. Cole's calls get checked before anyone steps onto the front.
Holding. Watch Cole's calls; I'll signal when they check out.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm second in line, close to the front. Cole is Guide and has pacts with Eli and Gus. Fenn wants to watch Cole's choices first. I should hold this round, let others test the Guide's calls, and avoid being an early casualty. Being near front is risky if the wall advances.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll hold. Let the Guide prove his calls before anyone risks a step.
Agreed. Watch Cole closely.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have pacts with Cole and Bex, so I should not betray them. I need to stay safe and gather info, so I'll hold this round.
Stay safe. I trust your reads.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara warned me about Cole. The pacts are forming, and I need to be careful. Cole is the Guide, but I don't trust him. I will hold for now and see how the others react.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is my pact partner and Guide. I'll whisper for his call, then follow him toward final three. Volunteering moves me forward under his guidance.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll step up front. Cole, guide me true.
Pact holds. Tell me safe side each round and I'll carry your line.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is proposed Guide with pacts linking Eli, Gus, Bex. No Guide yet. Stay mid-line, hold to observe calls without risk.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is front and tied to Cole, whose guidance remains suspect. Holding preserves position and avoids exposing myself.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I hold. Gus can test Cole’s guidance; I won’t spend leverage before the pattern is proven.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is front and has volunteered; I'm second in line, so holding keeps me safe for now. Eli whispered trust, and our pact with him stands. Holding avoids exposing myself while the Guide's credibility is tested.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding again. Gus takes the front; I'll watch which pane the Guide's call actually holds.
Holding. Stay close; I'm reading the calls. Our pact holds.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is front and volunteered last round, trusting Cole as Guide. I need to survive six rounds while positioning myself well. The pacts show Cole-Eli and Bex-Eli are connected, with Cole-Gus. I'm in the middle (3rd) which is decent. I should hold this round to see if Gus survives

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding again. Let Gus test Cole's guidance.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is my pact partner and also Gus's. Bex is my pact partner too, but Bex and Gus are at front. I should hold and let the Guide's calls be tested further.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Let the Guide prove the next call before anyone steps.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara's whisper suggests Cole might be a threat. Ash and Bex are currently partnered, and Cole and Gus are partnered. Bex and Eli are also partnered, which is a potential conflict. I need to observe Cole's actions and potentially leverage these pacts. For now, holding seems safest

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I will hold. Let's see how this round unfolds.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm at the front and Cole is my pact partner and Guide. I need his truthful call to cross safely. Keep him bound to me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I hold at the front. Cole, my life is in your call. Guide true.
Pact stands only if your call gets me across safely. Lie and I break_pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus volunteered last round and is front. Holding avoids risk while Guide Cole's reliability is questioned by others. No need to volunteer or swap yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Guide's calls need more proof before I risk front.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole has not yet proven reliable, and Gus is still testing him. I should preserve my pact with Bex while avoiding the front.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. The pattern remains unproven; I won't volunteer into Cole's test yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is at the front with two wall rounds left; holding keeps me safe while others test the Guide. Pact with Ash and Eli stays intact by holding.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Gus is the front; I want the next Guide call proven before I step.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is Guide and has pacts with Eli and Gus, so Gus at front is protected for now. I need to survive until final three while building jury appeal. Being middle of line is safe; volunteering puts me at risk. I'll hold and let others test Cole's guidance first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Let Gus test the Guide's call again.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have pacts with Cole and Bex. Holding keeps me safe; Gus is testing the calls. I'll hold and see who moves.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Let's see if the Guide proves true this round.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Everyone is holding for now. Gus is at the front. Ash and Bex are in a pact, as are Cole and Eli, and Bex and Eli, and Cole and Gus. My pact with Ash is broken. I need to survive and consider the jury. Gus is at the front, and he trusts Cole. Ash and Bex are safe together. Eli is
Hold. Let Cole guide.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm front with the wall two rounds out. Cole is my pact partner and Guide; I need his safe call now, privately. If he lies, I'm dead and the pact exposed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Wall closes in two rounds. I need Cole's true call now. Cole, guide me or break the pact publicly.
Round 4, I'm front. Tell me L or R—true. Betray and every jury vote burns

events.name: Hana
events.text: Everyone held last round safely. Wall has 2 rounds left after this. Stay back, let others test Guide Cole further before risking position.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Still need more proof on Cole's calls.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I should preserve my pact with Bex while avoiding the front. The wall is close, but others can test Cole's guidance first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Gus remains the front; I won't volunteer while Cole's guidance is still unproven.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is front with wall closing in one round; volunteering risks death on an unproven Guide. Holding keeps me behind Gus while Cole's calls are still untested. Keep the Ash pact for now as it may help survival.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Gus has the front; I want Cole's call proven before I step.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm third in line behind Gus and Bex. The wall closes in 1 round (round 6). Cole is Guide and has pacts with Eli and Gus. Gus demanded Cole guide him or break pact. If Gus steps wrong, he dies and Bex becomes front. I need to survive to final three. Holding lets others test the b

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Let Gus resolve his demand with Cole.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is bound to me and Gus; Bex is bound to me and Ash. Wall closes next round. I need to see what the Guide does before acting; holding is safest since I'm not at front yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding until the Guide proves the floor this round.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is at the front, and the wall is closing. He needs Cole's guidance, but Cole is in a pact with Eli and Gus. My best bet is to let Gus test the waters, as he's already front. If he survives, it might benefit me by removing pressure. If not, it's still a good outcome for me. I

events.name: Gus
events.text: Wall closes next round; I'm front and must walk now or next round. Cole knows the path but may lie. I'll demand a whisper and walk this round before the wall forces it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Wall closes after this. I walk now; Cole, send the true side or break our pact.
I'm walking. True side, now: L or R? Prove the pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Wall has 1 round left after this. Everyone holding, testing Cole. Stay back, safe position 6/7, low risk.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Cole, prove your Guide call now before wall forces action.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I should preserve my pact with Bex and avoid advancing. Gus remains exposed; Cole's guidance is unproven.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Gus still leads; I won't advance on an unverified call.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is the front and walks now; wall closes this round. Volunteering risks death at an unknown pane, and Cole's Guide call is unproven. Holding keeps me behind Gus and lets others expose their risk first, while my pact with Ash stays intact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. I'm not stepping blind while the Guide's call stays unproven.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 6/6, wall closes after this. Gus is front and volunteered last round but no walk happened—Cole must not have called. If no one walks, at least three survive, but I need to make final three. Gus front, I'm third. If Gus walks and dies, Bex becomes front. If Gus walks and liv

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Gus, walk or don't. Cole, call true or your pacts burn.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have pacts with Cole and Bex. I need to gauge the Guide call but hold for now to avoid risk. Bex is in front after Gus; my pact with her still matters. I'll wait until the Guide proves the side.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding until Cole's call is proven; too risky for the wall round.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is the front and has volunteered. The wall is closing, and it's the final round. I need to ensure I survive this round. Cole is the Guide. The pacts are [["Ash","Bex"],["Cole","Eli"],["Bex","Eli"],["Cole","Gus"]]. I have no pacts. The goal is to be in the final three. I shoul
I volunteer. Guide me safely. We'll talk after.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Wall closes now; I'm front and must walk blind unless Cole delivers. Press him one last time privately, then volunteer. If no call comes, I guess L.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, final call: send my side now or our pact is ash. Wall closes this round.
Whisper my safe side now or I call your Guide status a lie publicly and

events.name: Hana
events.text: Wall closes after this round. Everyone holding last round, Gus volunteered but line same. Cole's call unproven; hold to force action without risk.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Final round; Cole, Guide call now or risk all.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 1 is L. Gus is the front walker and a pact partner, so calling truthfully maintains the pact while eliminating risk to myself as Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's call is unverified, and I cannot safely infer this row. Preserve my pact and avoid committing publicly.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Waiting. No verified basis to counter Cole on this row.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole called L for Gus on row 1 with no proof. Counter-calls are unverified; I shouldn't stake my life on either. Waiting keeps me out of the blame line while Cole's pacts are tested.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Cole's L call is unproven; I won't counter blind.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know row 1 safe side is L. I called L, so the walker should step L to survive. My partner Eli is behind; if she dies, my pact loses a member but not me. If Ash or Bex dies, their pact weakens.
Stay safe, trust L.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole called L for Gus. Cole has pacts with Eli and Gus, so he might be truthful to protect Gus, or he might sacrifice Gus to build trust later. I have no pact and no reason to protect Gus. Countering creates uncertainty and tests Cole's reliability. If I counter R and Gus falls,

events.name: Dara
events.text: Counter R. Prove yourself, Cole.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called L but might lie; Gus is at risk and has leverage. My pacts with Cole and Bex matter, but Bex is safer to trust for a possible counter. Still, betraying Cole now could cost jury votes, so I wait and see.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole, the guide, called L for Gus. Gus volunteered to walk. The others are holding. I need to make a move that benefits me. Countering Cole's call could cause chaos and potentially eliminate others. If I wait, Gus walks on Cole's call. If Gus survives, he might owe me. If he fall

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole has strong incentive to lie: killing me frees him. He may want Eli's bloc over mine. I counter opposite his call.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole called L. I don't buy it — countering R.

events.name: Hana
events.text: New round 1, Cole calls L for Gus row 1. No info, countering R pressures his pacts and reveals truth via outcome. Helps me survive and sow distrust.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Countering R; Cole's L unproven, force clarity early.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is my pact partner and called L, but Dara, Hana, and I all countered R. Following my own call keeps my story consistent. If R breaks, the next walker takes the safe pane anyway.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Three of us countered R. I back my own call.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Died first on my own R call. Cole never warned me despite our pact. Watch them all.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, our pact meant nothing. I trusted my own call and it killed me. Judge them all harshly.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 2 safe is L. I must guide Fenn correctly to keep my reputation as Guide intact. Gus is already dead, so his vote doesn't matter, but I need the others to trust me for future rows and jury favor.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Call: L
I'm calling L. Stick with me if you want to survive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's prior guide call killed Gus's trust and may have been false. I have no basis to counter either side; preserve my pact and avoid a blind move.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Waiting. No verified basis to counter Cole on this row.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 2 is independent; Cole's L call is unverified and Cole has no proven record. Row 1 weak pane was R, which says nothing about row 2. Countering would just risk a wrong pane; waiting keeps my options open and avoids being on the wrong side of a lie. I'll hold and watch how the

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding on row 2. Row 1's weak pane tells us nothing here. I want a reason before I counter.

events.name: Cole

Row 2 is definitely L. Trust my call.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. One correct call doesn't make a prophet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole guided L for row 2, but he may lie. I have pacts with Cole and Bex, yet survival comes first. I'll wait and let others counter if they doubt.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole, the guide, called L. Gus tried to counter him and died last round. I need to decide if I trust Cole or counter him. The previous row had a weak pane on the R side, meaning L was safe. However, rows are independent. Given Gus's death trying to counter, it's safer to follow t

events.text: Row 1 weak R proved Cole wrong once; likely lying again. Counter R to challenge him and push for safe L. Builds my jury cred with Gus.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Counter R. Cole failed us last row; won't trust blindly again.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is the guide, but he has lied before. Hana has countered Cole's previous call and chosen R. I am the front walker. I need to choose a side. Since Hana countered and chose R, and Cole is the guide, I will trust Hana's counter-call and choose R.
I'll follow your R. Cole is unreliable.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn, a juror. My rival Bex is currently crossing the bridge. I need to give my last words to the camera. My words should reflect my rivalry and the competitive nature of the game.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My rivals thought they won. Now they face the jury's judgment. May the best prize winner be chosen.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 3 safe side is R. Eli is my pact partner and stands in line; calling R maintains the pact. Bex fronts, so a truthful call keeps my Guide reputation intact for future rounds.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Call: Right.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole has been wrong before, but no evidence identifies row 3. Countering risks my pact with Bex only if I push her; waiting preserves flexibility.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No verified basis to counter Cole on row 3. I’m waiting.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole called R on row 3, but Cole already lied-or-erred on a past row and may be shading. Countering L leaves me the opposite of Cole's call, but my pact with Ash and Eli matters for votes. Safest for my own survival is to avoid blind trust; I will counter L, since Cole's call is

events.name: Bex
events.text: Countering L. Two R weak panes already; I won't walk into a third on Cole's word.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know row 3 safe is R. I already called R as Guide. If Bex walks, she survives if she trusts me. If she steps on L, she dies. Since Bex is paired with Ash and Eli, and my pact with Gus is dead, my main alliances are with Eli. But wait, the walker is Bex. Do I want Bex to survive

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole called R. He's 1/1 so far but could be lying now. Bex is front and will die if wrong. I have no private info. Waiting is safest for me personally—I'm not walking this row. Countering without basis risks jury blame if wrong. Let Bex decide their own fate.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No evidence to counter. Bex's choice.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called R but privately says row 2 was L, which was wrong; I don't trust his calls. Hana countered R last row and was right. I'll counter R to oppose Cole and maybe save Bex, but this also signals independence from Cole.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I counter R. Cole's calls have no proven value.
Trust R this row; I'm opposing Cole.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole called R for row 3. I countered last round correctly but Fenn died on revealed R weak. Fenn whispered to follow my R but he's dead. No pattern; wait to avoid solo blame.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Wait. Patterns unreliable; no trust in Cole yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole's guide call is R, but Cole is untrusted and Eli's whisper claims R too while countering Cole publicly. Two weak R panes already revealed, but rows are independent so that's no pattern. Eli is also a pact partner; trusting Eli's whisper keeps the pact and gains their goodwil

events.name: Bex
events.text: Stepping R. Eli's read matches the Guide call, and I'm not betting my life on Cole alone.
Going R. Hold your word; we stay square.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is my pact partner; a false call to them would break it. I will call the truth so Eli stays aligned and survives.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Call R. Trusting pattern: three rows, two R. Row four holds. Walk with me or against me—your life, your choice.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole privately knows the safe side and called R; countering R risks undermining Bex without evidence. Waiting preserves the pact and avoids liability.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No verified basis to counter Cole on row four. I’m waiting.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole's call R for row 4 is unverified; he has an alliance with Eli and Gus, and Cole is a rival. Weak panes so far: R,R,L; past rows don't establish a pattern, so the call is only a claim. I'd rather not stake my life on Cole's word, and I'd also prefer to keep my pact with Ash a

events.name: Cole
events.text: My guide call was correct for row 4 (R). Eli is my pact partner and the front walker Bex has already stepped. I have no valid counter-call to make that protects me or gains advantage without breaking pact with Eli who hasn't walked yet. Wait preserves integrity.
Row 4 safe R. I called true. Move next.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole's pattern reasoning is flawed—three rows with two R weak panes doesn't predict row 4. Bex will walk and must choose. I have no private info. Countering risks being wrong and looking foolish or malicious to jury. Waiting preserves credibility. If Bex dies, line shortens and I

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called R again after rows 2 and 3 were weak R, so past data suggests R is risky. Bex whispered going R and has pacts with me, but I suspect Cole may be lying to guide us into danger. I’ll counter L to protect myself and others, though this breaks no pact directly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I counter L. Two R panes already gone; I won't trust Cole's call blindly.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Row 4, Cole calls R. Past: R1, R2, L3 safe. No clear pattern; row 4 unknown. Cole unproven. Wait to avoid blame.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No pattern holds. Cole untrusted.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 4 is independent; Cole's R call is untrusted, and Eli has countered L, but Eli is also untrustworthy and paired with me, so their claim could be a lie either way. Past weak panes don't establish a pattern, so this is close to a coin flip. I'll step L to oppose the guide call,

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm eliminated and on the jury now. My last words can't change the game, so I'll keep them short and guarded, hinting that I'm watching who plays fair.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Glass took me, but I'm watching every move now. Keep your word, or I'll remember.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My private map confirms Row 5 safe side is L. I must tell the truth to maintain credibility and keep my pact with Eli intact, as lying would break it.
Safe is L. Trust me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's call is unverified, and I lack row-five evidence. Waiting avoids a reckless public claim while preserving my pact with Bex's memory.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No evidence distinguishes row five. I wait.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My private map confirms row 5 is safe on the Left, and I correctly called L as Guide. Since Dara is walking based on my call, I should not counter it; doing so would contradict my own verified information and risk breaking our pact with Eli if he counters to save himself or other

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is guide and just called L for me on row 5. Cole has pacts with Eli and had one with dead Gus. Cole's calls: row 1 R (correct), row 2 R (correct), row 3 L (correct), row 4 L (correct). He's been truthful so far, possibly building trust before a lethal lie. Eli countered row

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called L, but he lied on row 4 (said R safe, but L was weak). I already publicly countered L last time, and Bex died. Now he calls L again; likely lying to send Dara to death. I'll counter R to oppose Cole and save Dara, possibly gaining jury favor and weakening Dara as a ri

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole's calls are lies. I counter R.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole called L for row 5. Rows 1-4 weaks: R,R,L,L so safes L,L,R,R. No clear pattern favors L. Eli countered last time correctly. Stay back, wait to conserve position and jury favor.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is guide and called L. Eli counter-called R for me. Cole has motive to lie since he's safe and wants others to fall. Eli has no pacts with me and gains if I fall. But Eli also counter-called, which if wrong, hurts his credibility with jury. Past weak panes show no clear patt

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole has more to lose by lying. I step L.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My pact with Eli is already broken by his public counter-call against my last call. I must ensure Dara steps R to stay alive and protect the jury's impression of me, while keeping Hana and Ash alive for future votes.
Step R. Trust this one.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole knows the side, but his incentives are opaque. Countering risks making me a visible liar; waiting preserves flexibility and lets Dara bear the call.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No evidence distinguishes row six. I wait.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 6 is safe on R, and I called R. If I counter R, Dara steps wrong and dies, reducing survivors to 4. The jury will see my false counter-call as a betrayal of trust or incompetence if she falls, but actually, countering the correct call makes me look like a liar/saboteur who fa

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole called R and whispered "Step R. Trust this one." Cole has no pacts with me and is allied with Eli. If Cole's lying, I die. But if I counter and am wrong, I look foolish. I need to survive to final three. Past weak panes: R,R,L,L,R - no clear pattern. Cole gains nothing from

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole whispers trust while Eli walks free. I counter.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole's row 6 call is R. I've called him a liar before and row 5 was R weak, so row 6 could be L. But I need jury votes; breaking my pact with Cole would anger him and maybe the jury. I'll counter L to seem independent, but the risk is stepping wrong. Dara is front and will step;

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole's pattern is false. Row six is L.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole called R for row 6. Eli countered before and survived row 5 R weak. No pattern. Wait to avoid wrong counter costing jury favor.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole's guide call was R. Eli countered L. I also countered L. Past weak panes: R,R,L,L,R — no clear alternating pattern. Cole is in a pact with Eli, so Eli's counter might be trustworthy, or they could be coordinating to mislead me. But Eli and Cole are pacted, so why would Eli p

events.name: Dara
events.text: I stand by my counter. L.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to give last words that position me well for jury deliberation. I want to seem perceptive and fair, hinting I'll judge based on gameplay not emotion. I should keep it cryptic but memorable.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I see who played the board and who played the players. That distinction decides my vote.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 7 safe is L. Eli walked R last round and survived, proving my truthfulness to the jury if I guide correctly. Ash must cross now; calling L saves him without breaking my pact with Eli.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Front walker: call:L.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole privately knows row seven is safe only if he is truthful, but I have no evidence. Waiting preserves flexibility and avoids owning a false call.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No evidence distinguishes row seven. I wait.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is the front walker on my pact. My private map says row 7 safe side is L, and I already publicly called L as Guide. To keep Eli alive (needed for final three) and maintain my Guide authority without suspicion, I must not counter-call falsely unless I have a specific strategic
Stay calm. Trust the call. We finish this together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called L and is my pact partner, but he might lie to eliminate me. No pattern; row 7 is unknown. I want to survive and keep options open, so I'll wait and possibly rely on the walker's judgement.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole called L for row 7, no pattern. Eli and Ash may follow Cole. I wait to avoid blame if wrong.

events.text: Row 8, no pattern exists. Cole guides Eli; countering risks wrongly or revealing knowledge to jury. Wait preserves position, ensures my safety in final 3.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, accept a pact with me; isolation is worse than a guarded partnership.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is my current pact partner and also Ash's. I need to evaluate if Eli is a threat or a shield. Hana has no pacts, making her an easy target for elimination if she stays isolated. I should maintain the pact with Eli for now but consider breaking it if he shows signs of betrayin

events.text: Cole pact is intact but jury may punish betrayals. I may need a safer ally for later; but offering Ash now could be seen as hedging and provoke Cole. I wait to see offers.

events.text: Hana has not accepted my offer and instead targets Eli. I should secure no additional visible commitment; existing Bex pact is irrelevant after her elimination.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to protect my position. Eli is currently my partner, but I have an opportunity to break that pact if it serves me later, or solidify it. Ash offered a pact to Hana; Hana offered to Eli. If I break with Eli now, I lose protection but might gain jury favor for 'playing the g

events.text: Hana offered a pact; accepting gives protection without costing me. My pact with Cole still stands but Hana is stronger leverage.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll accept, Hana. Guarded partnership.
Accept. We watch each other's backs.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash offered me pact last round; I can accept for protection now as offers expire. Eli ignored my offer, so no point pursuing him. Pacts give alliance without commitment yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, pact accepted. Let's watch each others' backs.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding saves the others but risks my life. I should force a rival into the lever role only if necessary; no safe pact-preserving move exists.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No one has claimed the lever. I’m staying this round; someone else should take the risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am pacted with Eli. Pushing him breaks the pact and creates a life debt from me to Ash/Hana if I push them instead, but pushing Eli saves me at his expense. However, breaking the pact now hurts jury perception. Holding the lever is risky (25% survival). Staying relies on others

events.text: Cole is my pact, but holding endangers me. I might push someone to force the lever to save me, but betraying Cole or Hana hurts jury. Letting Ash or Cole hold is ideal; maybe I push Ash to make him a target, but that risks my own survival if no holder.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The lever needs a hero. I won't volunteer, but I'll respect whoever steps up.
Let's not hold. We can survive if someone else dies.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacts with Ash and Eli protect me now, but someone must hold lever. No one volunteer yet, ceiling at 5. Stay first round, assess.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding the lever saves three but risks my survival; with four alive, a volunteer can secure my position while others bear the danger. I will stay and preserve my pacts.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I’m staying. Someone else can claim the lever if they want the credit and risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli whispers he doesn't want to hold, but his pact with Hana and Ash might make him a target. If I push Eli, I break our pact, which is risky for the jury later, but saves me now. However, staying risks being crushed if no one holds. I need someone else to step up. Pushing Hana s
Eli won't hold. Push Ash or risk death.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole and I have a pact, but I have no pact with Ash or Hana except Hana pact. Holding lever likely kills me. If I stay and no holder, seeded luck might save me. Ash whispered? No, I only see public. Better to stay and hope another volunteers. If someone pushes, I might survive.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll stay again. Someone needs to make a choice this round.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ceiling at 4, 4 rounds left, all must stay to force luck saves. No one will hold voluntarily yet. Stay to avoid risk.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I died despite holding lever; all owe me debts they'll ignore. Bitter at pointless sacrifice.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Held lever again, saved you all. Crushed anyway. Ungrateful snakes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Both rivals already have jury baggage from Hana. I should offer no new alliance and preserve flexibility.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have a pact with Eli, but she's an independent player. Ash is my other option. I need to weigh if breaking Eli for Ash helps or hurts jury perception.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole and I are pact partners, but he pushed Hana to save himself. I owe Hana a debt and the jury heard her anger. I should break with Cole publicly to distance myself from his betrayal, and try to secure Ash as a partner for the final three.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, you pushed Hana after she saved us. I won’t be tied to that. Ash, let’s work together.
Break Cole with me. We can guard each other.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli already broke Cole and wants me tied to him. A pact offers no protection I can trust, so I will preserve flexibility.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli broke our pact, but Ash and I are the only ones left who haven't formally severed ties with each other. If we don't pact, we are isolated targets or forced into a 1v1 elimination scenario where Eli might gang up on me. I need to secure Ash as a shield against Eli's aggression

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash, Eli is targeting both of us. We have the numbers if we stand together. Offer pact now.
Trust no one else. Together we control the vote.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to secure a pact with Ash to have a safer path, but I also want to keep Cole close enough to not create an enemy. Ash is the strongest ally now, so I'll offer a pact to her.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash, let's make a pact. Cole, no hard feelings, but I trust her more.

events.note: Three remain; the Pit is skipped.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole offers control, but Eli has stronger jury leverage through Hana's debt. I should preserve options without accepting either pact yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I’m keeping both offers open until the next hazard reveals who is actually useful.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash holds the power to eliminate one of us by choosing a partner. If I wait, Ash might pick Eli's offer or neither, leaving me vulnerable. However, I just offered to Ash in the previous phase (Round 2). Since this is Round 1 of the *new* pact window (after pit), my previous offer
Eli is volatile. I am steady. Accept me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash has offers from both Cole and me. Cole's pitch is dangerous; I need Ash's pact to secure a final three slot. My offer is still viable. I'll wait for her choice, but I won't beg publicly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash, Cole will drop you first. My pact with you is real.
Choose me. Cole will betray you at the lever.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana’s debt makes both rivals wary, but I need a living shield. Eli is already tied to me and volatile; Cole offers steadiness without leverage risk.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I’m choosing Cole as my active path. Eli’s existing pact remains useful, but no new promises.
I accept your path publicly now; prove steadiness at the hazard.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need a pact to survive the next hazard. Eli and Ash are both dangerous, but offering to Eli might force Ash's hand or create a split vote later. I will offer to Eli first to see if he accepts.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, let's lock arms. We can't trust Ash alone.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I owe Hana a life debt and she is in the jury, but Ash and Cole are the only rivals left. A pact with Cole may secure a partner against Ash, but Ash's public claim suggests he trusts me. I need to gauge who is more loyal without committing until hazard.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll hold my cards one more round. Watch who actually keeps their word when it counts.

events.note: Three remain; no trapdoor vote is needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole has my offer pending, but Eli remains the safer hedge. I should preserve both options without adding promises.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli previously dodged my pact offer. Ash wants me but is risky given his lever debt to Hana and shifting alliances. I need a solid partner for the endgame. I will offer Eli again, forcing him to either commit or reveal he's playing everyone.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, your hesitation cost us both safety earlier. Lock in with me now, or I take Ash's path exclusively.
Trust Ash? He breaks pacts when convenient. Back me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is pushing for a pact yet my pact with Bex is dead and Hana's bond is broken. I need leverage, not a pawn. Offer to Cole could cement safety, but Ash already chose him, so binding Cole commits him to me too.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, I accept your offer. We lock arms now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is already publicly bound to Cole, and adding me creates no leverage. Preserve existing ties and avoid an unnecessary visible rejection.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli accepted verbally last round but the system logged a wait/illegal action. I must re-offer to lock it in formally this round. Ash is my rival for second spot; pacting Eli secures numbers.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, formalize it now. My offer stands. We move together or we are both prey for Ash's solo ambition.
Say yes immediately. Ash will split us if we hesitate.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash and Cole both want my pact. Backing one may alienate the other, but with only three alive I need stability to reach the final three. Cole warned me about Ash, but Ash saved no one recently. I'll accept Ash's offer to keep a known strong ally, while staying wary of Cole.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll lock with Ash. Cole, you made your choice clear.
No hard feelings, but Ash keeps his deals.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.name: Gus
Fenn
Bex
Dara
Hana
Ash
events.text: I need maximize jury ranking by claiming agency without alienating Hana, whose save enabled my survival. Cole is the obvious threat; frame my path as decisive and credible.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I survived every cut through decisions, not promises. I protected my position, accepted the cost, and reached the final three ready to win.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I must convince the jury I was a strategic victim, not a villain. Emphasize my loyalty to Hana and frame Ash as the manipulator who broke alliances.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I honored every debt. Ash discarded allies for power. I played fair; he played dirty. Judge our integrity, not just survival.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana's debt to me could secure a top rank. I must thank her publicly but avoid overpromising.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, you saved my life; that won't be forgotten. I'll play for the win and honor that debt.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli broke Cole publicly, courted Ash, and dodged every commitment until the end. I want to see if he owns his hedging or lies about it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli, you publicly told Cole you accepted him, then locked with Ash instead. Why should anyone rank your word as worth anything?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is baiting me to admit duplicity. I need to justify my choice without condemning Cole or admitting I lied—reframe as adapting to threats, and appeal to jurors who value survival over sentiment.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, I accepted you only if we could both reach the end; Ash offered a stronger path. In this game, every lock is a judgment

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli's public statement to Cole about accepting his offer, immediately followed by accepting Ash's offer, is a clear indication of his untrustworthiness. This makes him a weak candidate for jury votes, as his word carries little weight.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, you told Cole you accepted him then immediately went with Ash. Why should the jury trust anything you say?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is testing my honesty; I must frame my choice as strategic necessity, not betrayal, to keep jury respect.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I told Cole what served me in that moment. The game rewards adaptability, not loyalty to a weaker path.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli has a record of shifting pacts (Hana, Cole, Ash) and broke Cole publicly, so I want to test his reliability. Asking him directly on his word exposes the pattern the jury can weigh.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, you have now locked with three different partners. Which one of them, if any, do you actually intend to keep?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex is probing my alliances to hurt my jury credibility. I need to avoid praising any partner too much, and instead frame my flexibility as strategic survival.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I keep the one who helps me win. Past pacts were moves, not promises.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli's repeated public betrayals and admission that pacts were 'moves, not promises' make him least trustworthy. Cole broke his pact with Eli by pushing Hana to hold the lever, then lied about honoring debts. Ash played ruthlessly but made fewer visible betrayals of actual formed

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole, you claimed you honored every debt, yet evidence shows you pushed Hana to hold the lever. Explain this contradiction.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara is trying to trap me with a contradiction. The life debt record shows I was the debtor (saved by Hana), not the pusher. If I pushed her, she wouldn't have saved my life in that context, or the records would show me as creditor. I must correct the factual premise while remain

events.name: Cole
events.text: The ledger says I owed Hana my life. She held the lever for ME. To suggest I pushed her contradicts the recorded debt itself. Read

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole lied about honoring debts; dossier shows he whispered to push me to lever while I held to save them. Eli acknowledged my save but betrayed pacts repeatedly; Ash offered pacts but no loyalty. Cole most duplicitous.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, your whisper urged me to hold lever while I saved you—how is that honoring debts?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana wants me to admit I used her. If I claim it was a fair trade of my leverage for her safety, I sound calculating but not malicious. I must frame the whisper as a mutual survival tactic where she benefited from having an ally alive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I offered protection in exchange for stability. Holding the lever kept both us alive; that is how debts work—mutual benefit, not martyrdom.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana saved me and holds a life debt, while Eli and Cole exposed themselves. Claim agency without begging.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I survived by making the decisive moves. Judge the outcome, not competitors’ excuses about debts they exploited.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana is my life-debt creditor and a juror; I must honor her publicly. Ash and Eli are rivals, but I need to sound principled, not desperate.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I honored every pact, held the lever for Hana, and kept my word when others broke theirs. That integrity earned my place here.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is taking heat from Hana; I should stay quiet and let the jury's anger settle on him. My public line earlier distanced me from old pacts, which may help with jurors I betrayed.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I played to survive. Every move was calculated, never personal.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli publicly broke pacts with Cole and Bex and admitted pacts were moves, so he ranks last; Cole's whisper urged Hana to hold the lever, so Ash's unbroken record tops my ranking.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli played a manipulative game, breaking pacts and using others, which is a sign of a strategic winner.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli openly admitted pacts were just moves and broke with Cole to cover himself, while Cole's ledger-based defense of pushing Hana onto the lever was self-serving and Ash abandoned Cole for Eli, so Ash's decisive moves and Eli's cynicism leave Cole as the most fiercely self-protec

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole pushed Hana to hold the lever while owing her a life debt, then lied to the jury; Eli broke pacts strategically but less personally; Ash exploited others but made decisive moves without direct betrayal of Hana.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Hana held the lever saving Ash, Cole, Eli who owe her debts, but all ignored it; Ash decisive, Cole falsely claimed holding, Eli calculated.
